metadata.name: hostname
metadata.displayName: hostname - Show or set system hostname

installation.note: hostname is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The hostname command displays or sets the system's hostname - the name that identifies the computer on a network. The hostname is used for network identification, system identification in logs, and is part of the system's fully qualified domain name (FQDN).

syntax.description: Display current hostname, or set hostname if HOSTNAME argument is provided. Setting hostname requires root privileges.

options.description: Print the fully qualified domain name (FQDN)
options.use_case: Get complete hostname including domain (e.g., server.example.com)

options.description: Print the IP address of the hostname
options.use_case: Get IP address associated with hostname
Get just the hostname without domain (default behavior)
Get just the domain portion of FQDN

output_explanation.notes: Shows the short hostname - just the computer name without domain information.

examples.title: Fully qualified domain name

output_explanation.notes: The FQDN includes both the hostname and the domain name, providing complete network identification.

examples.use_case: Get complete network identity for configuration or identification

examples.title: Get IP address
examples.description: Get IP address associated with hostname

output_explanation.notes: Returns the IP address that the hostname resolves to, useful for network configuration.

examples.use_case: Get system IP address for network operations

examples.title: Get domain name

output_explanation.notes: Extracts just the domain name from the FQDN, useful for domain-specific operations.

examples.use_case: Get domain name for configuration or scripts

elements.meaning: Change persists until reboot unless also configured in /etc/hostname

output_explanation.notes: Setting hostname requires root. The change is temporary - edit /etc/hostname for permanent changes.

misconceptions.title: hostname changes are permanent
misconceptions.misconception: Setting hostname with 'hostname newname' makes the change permanent
misconceptions.reality: hostname command changes are temporary and lost on reboot. For permanent changes, edit /etc/hostname and /etc/hosts, or use hostnamectl.
misconceptions.tip: Use 'sudo hostnamectl set-hostname newname' for permanent changes, or edit /etc/hostname

misconceptions.title: hostname is the same as computer name
misconceptions.misconception: hostname and computer name are always the same
misconceptions.reality: Hostname is the network name, which may differ from the computer's display name in some desktop environments. They're usually the same but can be configured separately.
misconceptions.tip: Hostname is primarily for network identification, not necessarily the same as GUI display name

common_pitfalls.description: hostname command changes are lost on reboot
common_pitfalls.solution: For permanent changes, use 'sudo hostnamectl set-hostname newname' or edit /etc/hostname and /etc/hosts

common_pitfalls.description: Changed hostname doesn't resolve to IP address
common_pitfalls.solution: Update /etc/hosts file to map new hostname to IP address, or configure DNS

common_pitfalls.description: Hostnames can only contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and dots
common_pitfalls.solution: Use only valid characters: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, hyphen (-), and dot (.)

related_commands.relationship: Modern alternative; hostnamectl is the systemd way to manage hostname permanently
System information; uname shows system info, hostname shows network identity

best_practices: Use hostname -f for FQDN in network configurations
Use hostnamectl for permanent hostname changes (systemd systems)
Update /etc/hosts when changing hostname to ensure proper resolution
Use hostname -i to get IP address for network scripts
Remember hostname changes with 'hostname' command are temporary
performance_tips: hostname is very fast - negligible performance impact
hostname -i may require DNS lookup, which can be slower
Cached hostname information is returned instantly

additional_notes.temporary_vs_permanent: hostname command changes are temporary. Use hostnamectl or edit /etc/hostname for permanent changes.
additional_notes.fqdn: Fully Qualified Domain Name includes both hostname and domain (e.g., server.example.com)
additional_notes.network_identity: Hostname is used for network identification and appears in system logs
additional_notes.valid_characters: Hostnames can contain: letters (a-z, A-Z), numbers (0-9), hyphens (-), and dots (.)
